subject: Request: DPA exception for encrypted-payload forwarding and subprocessor gating
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@medicom.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <contracts@medicom.io>
Date: 2028-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA: encrypted payload forwarding - ask for carveout

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our legal team reviewed the proposed DPA and raised a blocker: Section 4.2 disallows any forwarding of "payloads" to subprocessors unless the data is pseudonymized. Our analytics vendor requires periodic KV-cache snapshots to run their aggregation jobs — those snapshots would be end-to-end encrypted at rest, but the vendor needs the ability to decrypt using a customer-scoped key to compute derived statistics.

We're asking Redwood for a narrowly scoped exception: allow forwarding of encrypted KV-cache snapshots to a listed analytics subprocessor provided:
- the snapshot is encrypted with a customer-provided KMS key;
- keys are only accessible by the subprocessor via a short-lived KMS grant (no long-term key sharing);
- snapshots are logically segregated and access is logged to an audit bucket with proof of deletion within 30 days.

Attached: redline_dpa_medico_20280528.pdf and a diagram (kv_encryption_flow.png) that shows the proposed flow.

Can Product and Security confirm whether this is technically and operationally acceptable? Legal will need a short paragraph for the DPA amending Section 4.2 if you agree with controls.

Regards,

Sofia Ramos
Head of Data & Integrations
Medicom Health

Attachment(s): redline_dpa_medico_20280528.pdf (pdf), kv_encryption_flow.png (image)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-29T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: encrypted payload forwarding - ask for carveout

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear write-up and the diagram. Looping in Olga (Security) and Karthik (Product) for technical and product gating. Marcus, Hannah — legal and customer success: FYI.

High-level ask from our side: Legal will need a one-paragraph amendment if Security/Product can accept the controls. From Product: will this require any runtime changes (key material handling, logging hooks, feature flags)? From Security: what evidence do you need to be comfortable with a carveout?

I can push back to Medicom with two options:
1) We accept the carveout with strict KMS/HSM constraints + monitoring + deletion proof;
2) We deny, and Medicom must run analytics inside a customer VPC toy (their managed cluster) or use our hosted analytics add-on that runs under Redwood Dedicated.

Prefer to avoid option 2 if we can prove controls quickly. Olga/Karthik — can you triage? If you need any additional artifacts from Medicom please call that out and I'll request them.

Thanks,

—Priyom

Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-05-29T12:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA: encrypted payload forwarding - ask for carveout

Priyom / Karthik — read and quick technical readout: I can support a narrowly scoped exception but we need to harden the control set. My asks and notes below.

1) Key management:
- Customer must bring their own KMS (BYOK) with key policy that only allows the named subprocessor to decrypt via a short-lived grant (AWS KMS Grant or equivalent). No key material is escrowed by Redwood.
- We require that the subprocessor use a customer-scoped credential that is audited every access (request-level logs).

2) Access & segregation:
- Snapshots must be namespaced per customer and stored in a subprocessor-managed bucket with object-level encryption in transit+at-rest; Redwood must receive a signed manifest showing object checksums and TTL at handoff.
- We need proof of a segregation mechanism (folder-level ACLs, VPC isolation) — request their network diagram and an audit sample.

3) Monitoring & retention:
- All decrypt operations must emit an event into our ingestion pipeline; events are immutable and retained for 90 days.
- Subprocessor must attest to deletion within 30 days and provide deletion proofs (signed manifests). The evidence can be collected into the attached segregation_evidence.zip.

4) Operational constraints / fallback:
- If the subprocessor cannot support BYOK short grants, we require they run the analytics inside a customer-dedicated environment (Dedicated or on-prem).

If Medicom can provide: (a) KMS key policy draft; (b) network segregation diagram; (c) one week of sample access logs or the deletion proof artifact, Security can provide a conditional sign-off. Legal will still need language changes.

For Legal: propose a targeted amendment to Section 4.2 that: (i) enumerates the allowed artifact type ("encrypted KV-cache snapshots"), (ii) requires BYOK short-lived grants, (iii) mandates audit logs and signed deletion attestations, and (iv) limits the exception to named subprocessors in Schedule X.

Happy to hop on a 30m call with Medicom security to walk through controls.

—Olga
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-05-29T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA: encrypted payload forwarding - ask for carveout (Product asks & rollout)

Thanks — I reviewed Olga's checklist and the attachment. Product position and conditional sign-off below.

Acceptance criteria for Product sign-off (must be met before Legal drafts the DPA amendment):
- Engineering implements an opt-in feature flag on the tenant that toggles "allow-encrypted-subproc-snapshots". This gate must: deny snapshot exports unless the tenant has validated BYOK configuration and the Security checklist is marked complete.
- Runtime must emit a signed handoff manifest (tenant id, snapshot id, checksum, timestamp, target subprocessor id) that Security can query. Implement a retention policy for these manifests (90d).
- We require a minimal staging trial with Medicom (1 tenant, non-production data) for 2 weeks to validate the flow and deletion proof workflow.

Engineering effort estimate: 2 sprints (backend + KMS integration + manifest logs). We can prioritize next sprint if Legal and Sales agree to a targeted pilot timeline.

If Security confirms the checklist items are binary (yes/no) and Medicom provides the KMS key policy doc and one week of sample logs, Product will sign-off to allow Legal to craft the precise amendment language. Otherwise Product cannot accept broad language in the DPA.

Next steps (owner tags):
- Priyom: request KMS policy + network diagram + sample logs from Medicom (ASAP).
- Medicom: provide segregation_evidence.zip (attached) or equivalent.
- Olga: review artifacts and confirm checklist.
- Marcus/Hannah: Legal/CS to draft amendment clause and customer comms once Product/Security ok.

I'll also schedule a 30-minute sync for Wednesday to run through the pilot plan.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
VP Product, Redwood Inference
